fact: At fixed t0>0, g(x)=ut(x,t0)·dxu(j,x,t0) is smooth: the real inner product of two smooth Euclidean-valued spatial sections is smooth.
justification: ContDiff.inner with scalar ℝ and Euclidean codomain ℝ^m applies to the smooth sections supplied by N002 (also H002). This only accounts for routine regularity of the displayed product, not the integration-by-parts argument.

grounds.reason: ut and dxu are smooth on the positive-time domain; restricting to t0 gives smooth spatial sections.
t0>0 and j is a valid coordinate; g is explicitly the inner product of these sections.

fact: All fixed spatial partial derivatives of a smooth function on ℝ^n are smooth, in particular d=∂_{x_j}g; smoothness also supplies the coordinate-section derivatives used in M001.
justification: Apply the forward implication of contDiff_succ_iff_fderiv_apply at each finite order and at the jth coordinate unit vector. The scalar field ℝ is complete and ℝ^n is finite-dimensional. A partial derivative is exactly differentiation along this coordinate line; the function has the required differentiability, so the total-derivative convention agrees with the actual derivative. This is routine smooth-calculus bookkeeping.

grounds.reason: Joint smoothness at positive times yields all spatial derivative sections.
Smoothness of ut and dxu is expressly a conditional input.
g is the smooth product established by BG001, and d is defined as its jth partial.

justification: Apply HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact to each function. ℝ^n is Hausdorff, hence R1, and vanishing outside C says its nonzero support is contained in C. This just supplies the support guard used for M003.
